intent: Make a sieve's BAND into data the sieve carries — stamped into its declaration by the derivation that already computes it, read by the code that consumes it, and re-derived to check the declaration has not gone stale.
why: Akien, 2026-08-11, correcting CC's framing of his own bands-only ruling: 'bands only should make a disk change shouldn't it? it becomes part of the data attached to the seives, yes?' / 'and prolly in the code that consumes that data' / 'yeah, we gotta have both pieces!' THE LIVED SYMPTOM: today nobody can see a sieve's order without running an AST walk. The band is computed fresh on every run, attached to nothing, stored nowhere — so 'order is the band' is prose, and a reader who wants to know why a sieve fires third has to execute a walker to find out.
traces_to: Law 4 — a rule that matters is enforced by physics, not policy; 'order is the band' cannot be enforced against a band nothing carries. Law 3 — the band is an unmeasured claim recomputed in flight and never recorded. Law 7 — a stored band with no reconciler would be a record that can silently go wrong; the reconciler is what keeps it loud. Law 1 — the same AST walk is re-derived in every consumer, on every run.

the_ruling_that_shaped_it.the_acceptance_test_is_the_ruling: `cairn ruling verify 2026-08-11-one-mechanism-per-meaning` goes green exactly when all three named files have moved off their intake fingerprint AND Akien has confirmed. A mechanically-checked done-condition, derived from fingerprints rather than kept in sync by hand — nobody had to author it.

how: The derivation STAYS where ruling 2026-08-07 put it (import_sieve/sieve.py::reach_of — how far an import looks is that component's own domain) and takes two new jobs: STAMPER, writing the band into the sieve's declaration; RECONCILER, re-deriving to check the declaration still matches. Both consumers stop walking their own source and read the attached data. POLARITY, stated: the tester's (validation_store.source_fingerprint + standing) — MATCH means the declaration still holds, MISMATCH means the sieve's reach moved and the declaration needs an update. NOT the ruling store's polarity, where a match is the failure. OUT OF SCOPE, explicitly: any second way to express order, and any auto-restamp on mismatch (which would make the check vacuous).
falsifier: DONE when all FIVE hold, each by its instrument: (1) each sieve's band is READABLE FROM ITS DECLARATION without running an AST walk — instrument: a command printing every sieve's band from declarations only, with the walker not imported; (2) both consumers read the attached data — instrument: inspector.py:1722 and route.py:189 no longer call reach_of on their own source, verified by grep, with their proofs still green; (3) the reconciler catches a REAL drift — instrument: change a sieve's body so its reach genuinely moves a band, run the reconciler, and it names that sieve, its declared band and its derived band; (4) no second ordering mechanism exists — instrument: grep the declarations for any order/priority/sequence field, expecting zero; (5) A SIEVE IS A MODULE-LEVEL FUNCTION and a declaration that is not one is refused LOUDLY — instrument: point one declaration at a class method and one at a name that does not exist, run the reconciler, and it names both by name rather than banding them 0 (Akien's ruling, see a_sieve_is_a_function). HORIZON: (3) must be a drift from a real edit to a real sieve, not a fixture mutating a declaration to make the instrument fire.
wrong_intent: (a) The band becomes AUTHORED rather than stamped — hand-numbering back under a new name, inserting a sieve becomes a write to its neighbours (Law 6), and ruling 2026-08-06 has been quietly reversed. THE TELL: someone hand-edits a declaration.
(b) The reconciler AUTO-RESTAMPS on mismatch — the check can then never fail, which is the check that goes green for the wrong reason.
(c) The reconciler NEVER fires a mismatch across real use (ceremony) or fires constantly (noise, which gets trained away while still looking like coverage).
(d) A declaration is written that NOTHING READS — the half-built state where the data exists and the consumers still walk the AST. Strictly worse than today, because then there are two answers.

why_this_does_not_reverse_2026_08_06.what_that_ruling_killed: Hand-numbering the sieves, for two named defects (inspector.py's own comment): inserting a check 'would make inserting one a WRITE TO ITS NEIGHBOURS (Law 6)', and a derived band — unlike an authored one — 'cannot go stale'.
why_this_does_not_reverse_2026_08_06.why_a_stamped_band_carries_neither: The value is STAMPED FROM THE DERIVATION, never authored. Inserting a sieve writes that sieve's own declaration and no other, so there are no neighbour-writes. And staleness is precisely what the reconciler exists to catch, at the declared polarity.
why_this_does_not_reverse_2026_08_06.the_shape_of_the_answer: Persisted-but-derived is a THIRD option neither ruling considered. Derived-only (today) is unreadable; authored (killed) goes stale and writes neighbours; stamped-and-reconciled is readable, cannot be authored, and cannot silently drift.
why_this_does_not_reverse_2026_08_06.recorded_as: a distinction, not a collision — with the tell named above so a later reader can see it arrive if it does.

watchme.trigger: Every reconciliation — a re-derivation checked against a declaration. An event that fires by construction, since the reconciler is what this ticket builds. No clock, no sweep. Each firing reports per sieve: declared band, derived band, match or mismatch.
watchme.enough: When BOTH shapes have been observed across real use: at least one TRUE mismatch caused by a genuine edit to a sieve's body (the check can bite), and a steady state of matches between (it is not noise). One without the other is not enough — never disagreeing is ceremony, always disagreeing is noise; both are wrong-intent (c) and they are distinguishable only by watching over time. ALSO ENOUGH IN THE NEGATIVE: a mismatch observed being auto-restamped rather than surfaced is wrong-intent (b), and the watch has found the defect it was aimed at.
watchme.carrier: A verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier: per firing, the sieve name, declared band, derived band, verdict, and — on a mismatch — what changed in the sieve's body to move its reach. That last field is the payload; a count would be the count-instead-of-names failure probescan exists to end.

open_at_cast: WHERE THE DECLARATION LIVES, exactly. 'Attached to the sieve' is unambiguous about the RELATION and silent about the ADDRESS. A sieve today is a module-level Python function with a docstring; candidates are a sibling JSON file, a structured block in the docstring, or a decorator. The docstring option has precedent (the Provenance line lives there) and a strike against it: parsing prose for a number is the mention-not-capability failure sieve.py's own header records twice.
WHAT THE RECONCILER DOES ON A MISMATCH. Polarity is settled; the ACT is not. Red the build gate, raise a trouble, or report? Auto-restamp is NOT a free choice — it is wrong-intent (b).

DOES THE LADDER'S VERSION RIDE THE STAMP? Akien, 2026-08-11: a sieve 'is the best effort and will learn from experience.' The learning is not on the sieve's verdict (a rule is true or not) — it is on DEFAULT_LADDER, which its own comment calls 'a first cut (2026-08-06), not a settled taxonomy... Widening it is expected.' So a mismatch has TWO possible causes, needing opposite responses: the sieve's body moved (that declaration is stale, restamp it) or the LADDER moved (every declaration in the corpus is now off, and nothing is stale — the measure changed). Without a ladder version on the stamp those are indistinguishable, and a ladder widening reads as N stale sieves. A chart question, not a cast one.
DOES nest() CHANGE? Believed no (see measured_at_cast). If yes, cairn/tools/base/nest.py joins the ruling's what_conforms and the file list was short by one.

a_sieve_is_a_function.ruled_by: Akien, 2026-08-11, correcting CC at the cast
a_sieve_is_a_function.verbatim: a seive is a rule. it is true or not. it's the best effort and will learn from experience. why could it not be a function?
a_sieve_is_a_function.what_it_replaced: CC had flagged as a HOLE that reach_of walks module-level FunctionDef nodes only, so a sieve written as a method, a closure, or as data would silently receive band 0 — and had argued this got worse once the band was persisted. Measured after the ruling: ZERO such sieves exist (39 module-level functions and no classes in inspector.py; 11 plus one exception class in route.py). CC was proposing to widen the walker to shapes nothing uses — designing for complexity, walking past the simpler answer.
a_sieve_is_a_function.the_rule: A SIEVE IS A MODULE-LEVEL FUNCTION. Not a convention the walker must tolerate exceptions to — the shape of the thing.
a_sieve_is_a_function.the_code_already_assumed_it: reach_of's transitivity follows BARE-NAME calls only (sieve.py:173, isinstance(node.func, ast.Name)) — precisely how module-level functions call each other. The walk was never a partial view of a wider world; it was the whole world, correctly walked.
a_sieve_is_a_function.what_this_buys_at_no_extra_cost: The declaration this ticket builds IS the roster, so the rule becomes checkable by the reconciler already in scope: every declared sieve must resolve to a module-level function in its own module. Resolving to a method, a closure, or to nothing is LOUD — not band 0. A hypothetical hole becomes a real check (Law 4), for one more comparison rather than a new mechanism.
